note: The tool this add-on brings, the same text as aamio-python's aamio_domain_keys.mcp.TOOLS.

tools.name: aamio_addon_domain_check
tools.description: Check whether a website lists the key of a partner, or of a message this process read and verified. Give domain and exactly one of partner, a name in your address book, or message, the sha256 aamio_read showed. You never give a key: it comes from the address book or from the signature this process checked itself, so a message cannot pick the key that is compared, and a message read by an earlier process is not known here. Take the domain from the user, a contract or the address book, never from the message being checked: anyone can list their own key on their own site. Only websites on the user's own list are read. For any other the user is asked, in a form in their app, to type the domain themselves, and a domain they type differently stops the check. status is listed, not_listed, no_list, unreachable or invalid. listed is a dated observation that this exact website listed this key when it was read, and not permission to do anything: it does not say who holds the key, adds no partner and changes no allowlist. not_listed is no evidence of fraud, since a rotated key looks the same, and unreachable is never not_listed.

domain.description: the exact host, with no https:// or path. www.example.org and example.org are different places

partner.description: a name in your address book. Give this or message, not both

message.description: the sha256 of a verified message, as aamio_read shows it. Give this or partner, not both

name.description: the label the key should be listed under; leave it out for any. A label is a label and authorises nothing
